name: Lee Robinson
bio: Model research and personality at Cursor. Previously Vercel.

positions.claim: The bottleneck to reliable agent outcomes is orchestration and behavior, not model intelligence.
RLMs are the next paradigm of test-time compute, unifying reasoning and tool calling.
An unmodified default RLM harness performs comparably to a top-10 purpose-built memory system.
Qwen 3.5 9B run as an RLM beats Opus and GPT-5.4 run as plain LLMs on the Long CoT benchmark.
The ARC Prize team's refusal to run the full private evaluation for Symbolica's RLM harness result was unjustified.
Benchmarks should maintain a separate open-harness leaderboard rather than excluding RLM results outright.
It does not matter whether performance comes from latent space, reasoning tokens, or code execution — only results matter.
A system only qualifies as an RLM if the model itself chooses the decomposition; hardcoded map-reduce pipelines like lambda RLM do not qualify.
Claude Code was not an RLM before dynamic workflows, but with dynamic workflows it now arguably is.
Coding agents are not automatically RLMs, though they can be made into them.
Any coding agent with a file system and sub-agents can be converted into an RLM using OpenProse, without depending on Claude Code's dynamic workflows.
Capturing a successful 'golden session' as a reusable declarative workflow is a viable route to making agent performance repeatable.
Trust in an agent is reducible to its reliability.

Public evals systematically overstate model capability because models mine Git history and the web for answers; simple controls like deleting Git history and network allowlists noticeably change reported scores.
An eval where all models score around 90% should be retired, and eval half-life shrinks as models get smarter, so eval creation must be a continuous investment.
There is market room for a model that is fast, smart, and cost-effective alongside the most intelligent frontier models, and both types should be offered.
Training on an open-source base (Kimmy) limits control, so a full pre-train from scratch is the right next step.
Deleting features from generated applications until tests fail is an effective and scalable way to produce hard, verifiable RL problems.

Textual feedback — a teacher model hinting at a specific rollout step and reweighting probabilities — is more precise than end-of-rollout grading and generalizes to arbitrary behaviors, not just tool calling.
Most models today cannot reconstruct an incident fix by reading Datadog logs, Slack, and Notion the way a human engineer would.

Once compute is abundant enough for multiple simultaneous large runs, the binding constraint becomes the humans training models, so automating monotonous research work is the highest-leverage investment.
Agent-to-agent collaboration, with humans supervising teams of agents, will be a major trend within the next six months.
The overall training system is bottlenecked on the intelligence of the smartest model in it, because every judge, reward model, and research agent is distilled from it.
Agents will need their own persistent artifact store — a 'Dropbox for models' — since code repositories are a poor fit for non-code work products.
Cursor is close to shipping a new model that will be a notable improvement over Composer 2.5.
